description: Salmon Science - Stream Temperature Monitoring is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Cook Inletkeeper; University of Alaska Anchorage | Alaska Natural Heritage Program; USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. This interactive site describes how warming stream temperatures are affecting salmon. The site also discusses potential solutions. The project's monitoring network works to collect consistent, comparable temperature data for Cook Inlet’s salmon streams. They use these data to document the rate of stream temperature increases and areas where threshold temperatures are crossed throughout the watershed. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Water Quality. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Cultural and Community Services, Economy, Natural Areas and Wildlife. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
